name: Agent Voice
author: duaneoca
description: Wake word, spoken replies, and the knobs that govern them, for whichever AI agent is on the box.

barWidget.description: Hot-mic state at a glance, the last thing it heard, and live control over the timings that decide when it starts and stops listening.

schema.label: Wake phrase
schema.description: Pinned by a Vosk grammar. Every option here was measured on this machine: all detect reliably and none false-woke across 98 seconds of ordinary speech. "hey omarchy" is absent because Vosk's lexicon has no such word and it never fires.

schema.label: Microphone gate (dBFS)
schema.description: Guards the Vosk grammar and decides when your turn has ended. It does NOT gate openWakeWord, which scores every frame -- gating that one discards most of the phrase.

schema.label: Wake word confidence (%)
schema.description: How sure the recogniser must be before the trigger counts. The grammar has to choose between the phrase and anything-else, so near misses score as matches; this rejects them.

schema.label: Time to start speaking (ms)
schema.description: How long you get to begin after the wake word. Raise this if you feel rushed. It stops counting the moment you make a sound, so it never competes with the trailing pause.

schema.label: Pause that ends a turn (ms)
schema.description: Quiet time that means you have finished. Raise if it cuts you off mid-thought.

schema.label: Discard shorter than (ms)
schema.description: Anything briefer is treated as a false wake and thrown away.

schema.label: Hard ceiling (ms)
schema.description: A stuck open microphone stops here rather than recording forever.

schema.label: Transcription model
schema.description: tiny.en is the measured default on 2014-era hardware: 4.9% WER with the vocabulary prompt at ~320ms. small.en costs nearly two seconds per turn.

schema.label: Speak replies aloud
schema.description: Piper text-to-speech. Off leaves replies as text only.

schema.label: Voice
schema.description: Piper voices, all measured around 22x realtime on this hardware. lessac and amy are female, ryan, joe and hfc_male are male; low is faster and thinner than medium.

schema.label: Deaf period after speaking (ms)
schema.description: The microphone ignores everything for this long after the voice stops, so room reverb and the audio buffer's tail cannot be mistaken for you talking. Raise it in a room with hard walls.

schema.label: Wake word engine
schema.description: vosk takes any phrase but scores phonetic neighbours as high as the real one; openwakeword has four phrases and real rejection.

schema.label: openWakeWord phrase
schema.description: Only these four ship pretrained. Any other phrase has to be trained.

schema.label: openWakeWord threshold (%)
schema.description: Measured here: real phrase ~99, phonetic near-miss ~90, unrelated speech ~0.

schema.label: Keep listening after a reply
schema.description: Carry on without repeating the wake word. Say 'stop', 'cancel that' or 'never mind' to end the exchange, or just stay quiet.

schema.label: Follow-up window (ms)
schema.description: How long it keeps listening after speaking before it needs the wake word again.

schema.label: Live transcript while you speak
schema.description: Rough text shown as you talk, before Whisper returns. It needs the Vosk model, which costs 156MB resident. 'auto' shows it only when Vosk is already loaded for the wake word, so it is never paid for twice.
